newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MAKE SOLID START WITH HAYDEN AND ELLIOTT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA MAKE SOLID START WITH HAYDEN AND ELLIOTT.

text.p: Australian captain Mark Taylor's miserable run of form continued on the second day of the first test against South Africa on Saturday but he was the only morning casualty as the touring side reached lunch on 93 for one wicket.
Taylor was bowled off an inside edge by Shaun Pollock for 16 when the total was 33 and has now gone 16 consecutive test innings without reaching 50.
Taylor played back to a full length delivery and departed having faced 35 deliveries and struck two fours through the gulley region.

Fellow left handers Matthew Hayden, who opened, and Matthew Elliott grew in confidence and stature as the session progressed but the home side's much lauded pace attack never did themselves justice on a largely erratic and wayward morning.

Chief culprit was Allan Donald, expected to be South Africa's main weapon, who delivered an opening spell of four overs that contained two wides and several more deliveries that might have been called wide.

Elliott (36 not out) was the more aggressive of the two batsmen dominating the second wicket stand of 60 and showing considerably more skill than Hayden (37 not out) in reading the wrist spin of Paul Adams who bowled three overs before the break.
